claim.claim-text: 1. A prosthetic pericardial valve which comprises an expandable tubular stent having an annular collar and an internal leaflet assembly, wherein the stent is covered on an exterior surface with stabilized tissue, synthetic fabric material, or a combination of both, and the internal leaflet assembly is disposed with the lumen of the stent and is comprised of stabilized tissue, synthetic fabric material, or a combination of both, wherein the annular collar is a web of polyester or polyester-like fabric or metal mesh spanning from a distal end of the stent body to a collar support structure made from superelastic metal, the collar forming a flat circular band connected on one edge to the stent and extending radially around the exterior of the stent at or near a distal end of the stent.
2. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the internal leaflet assembly is saddle-shaped.
3. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the stent covering is stabilized tissue.
4. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the leaflet assembly is comprised of stabilized tissue.

5. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the prosthetic pericardial valve is elastic and is compressed into a delivery catheter for deployment within a patient, and whereby upon expelling the prosthetic pericardial valve from the delivery catheter, the valve expands to its functional shape.
6. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the stent and collar support structure are formed from the same piece of superelastic metal.
7. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 6, wherein the superelastic metal is a nickel-titanium alloy.
8. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 7, wherein the stent and collar are laser cut with pre-determined shapes to facilitate collapsing into a catheter delivery system.
9. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the stent is constructed from ductile metal that requires a balloon for expansion once the valve is positioned at the valve annulus.
10. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the stabilized tissue is derived from 30 day old bovine, ovine, equine or porcine pericardium, or from animal small intestine submucosa.
11. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the synthetic material is selected from the group consisting of polyester, polyurethane, and polytetrafluoroethylene.
12. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the stabilized tissue or synthetic material is treated with anticoagulant.
13. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the stabilized tissue or synthetic material is heparinized.
14. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the angle of the collar to the stent comprises a range of between about 5 and about 45 degrees.
15. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the collar extends laterally beyond the wall of the expanded tubular stent between about 2 and about 20 millimeters.
16. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the tubular stent has a plurality of tether attachment structures.
17. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, further comprising a plurality of tethers attached to the prosthetic pericardial valve for anchoring the prosthetic pericardial valve to tissue.
18. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 17, wherein at least one of the plurality of tethers is an elastic tether.
19. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 17, wherein at least one of the plurality of tethers is a bioresorbable tether.
20. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 17, wherein at least one of the plurality of tethers is a positioning tether and at least one of the plurality of tethers is an anchoring tether.
21. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, further comprising at least one tether attached to the collar support structure and at least one tether attached to the stent body.

22. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, further comprising a plurality of tethers attached to the prosthetic pericardial valve wherein one of the plurality of tethers is attached to an epicardial tether securing device.

23. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the leaflet assembly is constructed solely of stabilized tissue or synthetic material without a separate wire support structure, wherein the leaflet assembly comprises a plurality of valve leaflets attached to a leaflet housing, wherein the leaflet assembly is disposed within the lumen of the stent and is attached to the stent to provide a sealed joint between the leaflet assembly and the inner wall of the stent.
24. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the valve has a three-dimensional structure that is a D-shape in lateral cross-section.
25. The prosthetic pericardial valve of claim 1, wherein the valve has a three-dimensional structure that is a kidney-shape in lateral cross-section.
